keyVerseDR: "He that ruleth his spirit, is better than he that taketh cities." (Prv 16:32)

level1.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Self-Control
level1.story: Self-control means being the boss of your feelings and actions. You can wait, breathe, and choose!
level1.keyLine: I can stop, breathe, and choose.
level1.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice self-control all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: When did we use self-control this week?
What helps us calm down when we are upset?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level1.prayer: Holy Spirit, help me control my words, feelings, and actions. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Take three deep breaths when upset
TUE: Wait your turn without whining
WED: Turn off the screen when asked
THU: Save a treat for later
FRI: Use calm words when angry
SAT: Go to bed on time

level2.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Self-Control
level2.story: Self-control means guiding our feelings and actions and holding back impulses. When we feel angry, greedy, or impatient, we can stop, breathe, and choose what is right. Proverbs says the person who rules his own spirit is stronger than a soldier who captures a city! Self-control is a fruit of the Holy Spirit, and it grows each time we practice saying a good 'no.'
level2.keyLine: I can stop, breathe, and choose.
level2.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice self-control all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: When did we use self-control this week?
How did God help us grow in self-control?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level2.prayer: Holy Spirit, help me control my words, feelings, and actions. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Give up a snack or game for a day
TUE: Count to ten before reacting
THU: Keep your voice calm in an argument
FRI: Limit screen time and play outside
SAT: Offer a small sacrifice to Jesus
